utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of the Prosecution, I'm Tom Hannis, with Gerard Dobbyn and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. For the Zupljanin Defence, Aleksandar Aleksic. I would also like to inform the Trial Chamber that our client will not attend the trial today during the day, his written approval is expected for the trial to take place without his presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. And if there are no preliminary matters, could the witness be escorted back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Andan. Before Mr. Zecevic resumes his examination-in-chief, I remind you of your solemn declaration. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If the Usher would be so kind to please hand over the other binder to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Andan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, we broke off on Friday while we were looking at the first few pages of your notes. The document is 65 ter 831D1, tab 59.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the fourth page of the Serbian text. Could we please get page 4. I suppose in English it's page 2. The section where the date is 20 July 1992. The following page in Serbian -- or actually it's the same page but the right side. But in English it should be the following page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, this entry is dated 20 July 1992, and it reads: "Meeting with the prime minister Djeric ..." Tell me, did Dr. Djeric come to Bijeljina on that date and did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see from this text, he was on a two-day visit in Bijeljina and I spoke to him twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What was the topic of your conversation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke at Dvorovi, which is a neighbourhood near Bijeljina. You can see who else was present, and we discussed the security situation in the Bijeljina municipality. We acquainted Mr. Djeric with all our activities and the activities planned for the coming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djeric support you in your efforts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we got full support from him. And he said that we must finish the work we had started. We complained to Mr. Djeric that we had minor problems with the political structures in Bijeljina. We asked him to use his authority on the meeting that was planned for the following day, that is, the 21st, at the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina to assist in resolving the trouble that we had, and the paramount cause were paramilitaries, and that was the same in all of Republika Srpska. If you take a look at the relevant entry, then you will see that he insisted that full legitimacy be given to the bodies of the MUP and he fully backed up the police structures of Republika Srpska. I can give you an example of the situation in Bijeljina at the time. Mr. Djeric had doubts about safe accommodation in Bijeljina, and I offered him to spend the night in the house that I used at the time, and that's what he did. A Bosniak house was given to me to use there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since you've mentioned this, tell me, who else lived with you in that house at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived there with my wife and two children at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following page of the Serbian text. We don't need to change the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment on this entry of yours, the underlined part that are supposedly the words of Mr. Djeric. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I mean the last sentence on this page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric basically confirmed what we had come for, because there were some doubts about paramilitaries and the self-styled Chetnik Vojvodas and their units with regard to the way we arrived. There may have been some doubts in political circles why we had come to Semberija and Majevica. And he confirmed that we were there pursuant to the order of the government, or, more specifically, since the minister was a member of the government and we were there pursuant to his orders. A conclusion must have been reached by the government for the minister to exercise his authority and deploy us in an area that, according to their assessments, was -- was facing much trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you used the pronoun "us" in your answer, do you mean the unit of Mico Davidovic and the other units that were sent to Bijeljina to assist in the resolution of the situation there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Apart from the police forces, and I mean Mr. Davidovic's forces and Malovic's forces, we successively received reinforcements from operatives because we needed them, too, in some phases of our work. And Mr. Danilo Vukovic was also appointed chief of the crime enforcement service in Bijeljina because there was a shortage of personnel. I'm referring to crime police that had come from outside, that were not locals from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us comment on the following page of your notebook. The title is "Working Meeting."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're still on the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment what this working meeting was about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. We were trying to introduce a pre-war practice even under such difficult circumstances in war; namely, something that was done weekly and once a month there was a summary meeting. And at those meetings we analysed our work, both successes and failures, and we would reach conclusions for our future work. This was one of the working meetings of this kind where we analysed the activities in the previous period. We also touched upon our duties for the coming period. And since the highest-ranking officer chaired this working meeting and since he was involved in all our problems in Bijeljina, it was only logical for Mr. Cedo Kljajic to chair the meeting. I didn't go into the minutest detail of all the discussions, but I mentioned the main topics of the meeting in bullet points, as well as our conclusions with regard to the focus of future activity. You can see here that 80 men were received from other areas. Some 80 MUP members of the then Bosnia-Herzegovina who were Serbs had fled Tuzla and other municipalities that were controlled by the BH Army. At one meeting we decided to give them employment with the MUP, so we admitted these people who had been vetted, others had been -- others were subjected to a vetting process. In the initial stage, we removed some 40 police officers. And in August, or round about August, these latter officers were re-admitted, upon which some internal problems ensued, but I can comment on that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of the Serbian text, on the next page actually, could we look at the second bullet point. It starts with the word "preventing." Can you tell us briefly what this pertains to? It's the same meeting.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were constantly facing the problem of the activities of the paramilitary forces, and this is a continuous struggle against this plague that had affected all of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I mean, after the war I found out that they also - I mean, when I say "they," I mean colleagues from the Federation - had the same problem. So I say that we continue to struggle against the paramilitaries. I said organisations here, but they are formation, units. And also I refer to organised crime. I've already spoken about that and I think that that is contained in some of the written information I've provided, namely that all these formations that have come had one single objective, not to protect the Serb people. They came to loot, to rape, and to cross the border with their booty. That way their "warfare" would be brought to an end. Once they needed more things, they would come back to the same area and go on looting, the same problem all over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just the last entry now, could you please tell us what that pertains to, establishing responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I already talked about. That was mentioned here by way of a footnote. Please don't take my word for any date once again; I am really not very good with dates. But I know what periods are involved; I know how things happened, in cycles. A dispatch arrived from the Ministry of the Interior, perhaps it did not, but at any rate at this work meeting we underlined that once again the responsibility of all those who had committed a crime had to be established, even those who had committed misdemeanours, but the rules of service prohibit even that kind of thing for law enforcement officials. So we made a clear differentiation between those who worked hard and those who were lazy, those who were criminals, I can say that quite openly, when who had wore uniform and those who did not. During these times of war, in some magical way they managed to get into the Ministry of the Interior; however, we identified them and got rid of them as soon as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next entry says the 23rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is page 8 in e-court of the Serbian text. I assume that it's page 4 in English. Next page, please. It is page 3 in English, I've just been told, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the date is the 23rd of July, 1992, and the heading says "Discussion on going to Brcko." Can you give us your comment. Can you tell us whether this has to do with that trip to Brcko that you told us about on Friday, the one that you testified about on Friday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the period involved. I don't want to repeat what I've already said. We had received information which we later checked on the ground, namely that these paramilitaries had threatened the security situation there; I mean, they attacked even the public security station. So you can see that on the 23rd of July, 1992, with 110 policemen, we went to Brcko to reinforce law and order and to do away with crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page we see the 24th of July, 1992, Brcko. Please take a look at this. We don't need to repeat any of the things you said on Friday, but does this pertain to what you already told us about, the situation that you found in Brcko and the clash with the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the period involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us please move on to the 25th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is page 13 in the Serbian version. I assume it may be page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is the 25th of July, 1992. The heading says "Discussion of the Bijeljina CSB about problems in Zvornik." Tell me, can you give us a comment in respect of this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On several occasions we received information from several sources stating that the security situation in the territory of the municipality -- not only the municipality of Zvornik but the city of Zvornik itself in particular was threatened by an individual nicknamed Zuco. He was in charge of Zvornik, legally and formally. Before this official discussion, at a morning meeting we analysed the information that had come in, and it was agreed that I together with two or three men, one operative, that is, and two members of this unit, I think that they were members of Mico Davidovic's unit, that we change into civilian clothes and enter Zvornik and observe everything that we were interested in from a security point of view. That is indeed what we did. We entered the town of Zvornik. We observed all the buildings --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You already testified about that on Friday in relation to the previous entry in your diary. However, in relation to this particular entry, could you give us a comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious here that we had already had sufficient information, and we tried to agree on how this paramilitary formation could be neutralised. You see here that Zuco entered the TO Staff premises and the municipality and for a while he kept prisoner even the representatives of the authorities and the Territorial Defence in that he basically dictated the overall situation in Zvornik. We had to oppose that in an appropriate manner. This has to do with a work meeting to which we invited the commander of the Eastern Bosnian Corps, Mr. Ilic. Now, this Blagojevic, whether he was his Chief of Staff or not, that is something I don't know now. But we tried to discuss this with the military so that they would deal with these paramilitaries, not only the Yellow Wasps. On Friday we discussed Splico and some other paramilitary formations that were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move on to page 15 in the Serbian. I assume it's the next page in English. "Discussion in the SO Bijeljina, the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly." That is the title of that particular entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us your comment on the second bullet point underneath this heading "Discussion in the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to regular information that was provided to the Ministry of the Interior, of course there were periods when there were no radio, teleprinter, and telephone communications, then we sent information by courier at least once a week. We regularly informed political structures of government about the situation in Bijeljina. Our aim was quite simply to get the political authorities involved in resolving this problem so that we could do that as quickly as possible. We said, whenever we reported, that no stability could be achieved if paramilitaries were there. This did yield some result, and we were invited to a meeting at the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly and the situation in Bijeljina was discussed. It wasn't good at the time. You can see here that at that meeting we assumed responsibility, although it was not our duty according to the law, to protect various persons, namely the assemblymen from the territory of Bijeljina. That is to say that we made every effort for this problem of security to be raised to a higher level, to galvanise the Government of Republika Srpska into action through Bijeljina in order to stop the paramilitaries from coming into Bijeljina from Serbia. Unfortunately, that did not happen, and we did not fully achieve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, there is an entry here, "Dragan Djordjevic." And then it says "Crni" under quotations marks, so it's just his name, surname, and nickname. Can you give us your comment on this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I mentioned him on Friday, that that is also a member of a paramilitary formation. Now, was he in Samac? I think it was in Samac. There were two extremes in these paramilitary formations, Crni and Lugar. We thought that in the coming period, with the forces that we had available, of course, again, not at our own initiative but with the approval of the minister and his subordinates, we enter Bosanski Samac and disarm these paramilitary formations. I don't know what the next objective was, whether criminal reports could be filed and so on, however I note that was the first time I heard that name and surname and that's why I recorded it in my diary at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page, please, both in Serbian and in English. It is the 31st of July, 1992, and it says "Work Agreement."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about this? It has to do with the implementation of the Zvornik operation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Although we then had contacts with the National Security Service in Zvornik that was headed by the late Zugic at the time, Goran Zugic, we probably hadn't received all the intelligence that was relevant for our plan, so we kept meeting until the operation actually started. I think that this has to do with going to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I need page 18 now. The 2nd of August 1992 in Zvornik. The next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, it says: "Zvornik informing the minister of the Serb MUP about the overall security situation in the area of the municipalities of Bijeljina, Brcko, Zvornik, the 2nd of August, 1992." Did this information -- was this information provided after the Yellow Wasps were arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. After completing this operation - and that was done very successfully I must say; there weren't even any casualties involved; I don't think that anyone was even seriously injured - we sent a report on the action that had taken place. In the meantime, Mr. Stanisic was announced and did appear there and we were supposed to provide him with information about the overall security situation. To be quite frank, he was interested about certain colourful details, like how policemen came to the 6th and 7th story of buildings using ropes; that's where the paramilitaries were and how they were ultimately overcome. So we told him about all of that. At the end of this two-hour meeting with the minister, he paid tribute to our efforts and he said that we should continue along those lines and said that the problems that other municipalities were facing also called for such units, or perhaps we could quite specifically be in the focus and perhaps we would have to count on that, dealing with paramilitaries and criminals not only locally but throughout the republic. I think that what was being intimated at the time was our transfer to Foca that was also facing a great many problems, like Zvornik. That is where local criminals were basically running the municipality of Foca and we were supposed to establish law and order there, but this was just by the by. We were being informed about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And I would appreciate your giving us a comment. Can you tell us whether this meeting was held in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was held on the premises of the police station in Zvornik. There was a nice conference room there that could house some 20 or so people. It was a conference room and that's where we met with Minister Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page of this entry, we can see that it says that there was a dead-line given and the dead-line was the 3rd of August. Could you tell us what that relates to? It is the second bullet point on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a short investigation that we carried out after the arrests of the paramilitary unit, we learned that some of the leading officers, even the police station commander, komandir, had in fact taken part in criminal activities, and quite a lot, and that Zuco, in fact, in effect had control over the police station by way of their commander. We informed Minister Stanisic of this and this problem and he said that by 3rd of August everyone who was involved in any type of criminal activity that we could document should be processed, that the criminal report should be submitted to the Prosecutor, and that they would be issued a decision on the cessation of their work for the police station. So we informed the minister of the situation at the Zvornik Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will see in a moment a document relating to that. Now, on the next page, on the right-hand side of the page which we can see on the screen now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I don't know if you will be coming back to the response that the minister gave to the information offered by the witness, but maybe you would take this opportunity to ask if there was a response, indeed, from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, I wasn't checking the transcript, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The witness just told us that he made sure that the minister was informed about the problems in Zvornik. That's a useful piece of information. And I would be curious to know if the minister responded to this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely -- he said, on page 13, line 20: "... he said that by 3rd August everyone who was involved ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that, because this is the entry in his notebook, that it refers to the minister. And that is how I understood it, that the minister said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I probably misunderstood. I'm sorry for that. So this was the minister's response; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was the minister's response. And if you allow, I can expand on this by giving some additional explanation. Can I do that? Legally speaking, the chief of the security centre was responsible for the entire proceedings involving taking disciplinary action and submitting criminal complaints within the centre that he was responsible for. Now, the chief of administration was in charge of inspectors, and the chief of the crime administration was also responsible for his own employees within the crime police. Now, the minister could, pursuant to a proposal by the chief of an administration, take action against chiefs of centres. So that was the procedure. And I understood the order issued by the minister at the time that we should take all necessary activities to eliminate all those individuals for whom we could find evidence that they were involved in criminal activity and that they were -- that they had some ties with the paramilitary unit of the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I move on, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the right-hand side that we have on our screens, now we have the third bullet point beginning with the words "paramilitary units." What I would like to discuss now is that bullet point. And then there's another bullet point where it says at ... "on pain of death." So could you please comment these two bullet points.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we are talking about what we were to do next, in other words, a total and full sorting out of the situation with the paramilitary units and getting rid of them. So this was something, a task that we assumed, and there was no dead-line because it was impossible to say whether this could be done within a month or two, but this was an on-going task that we had. And finally, I said here that on the pain of death, all of this had to be handled. So all of those tasks that we had discussed, such as disarming and putting all the paramilitary units under authority, under some legal command, the restructuring of -- restructuring or, rather, clearing all our ranks as it were of all those who had managed to insinuate themselves into our ranks and getting rid of them if they were criminals, and all of those who had actually abused their powers as police officers should be processed. Against some there would be disciplinary action taken. And against others, criminal action would have to be taken. But this would have to be done on the pain of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one small question: Was that the position of the minister as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I don't know how well you know Mr. Stanisic, but he was a person who could be very, very decisive. Sometimes he would even actually conduct himself almost as a military person. That was one of the personality traits that he had at the time, and he was the one who said, you know, this has to be dealt with on the pain of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the entry for the 4th of August, 1992, Bijeljina SJB. In English, that will be on the next page. Perhaps we can -- maybe it's on the next page. I don't know. The English version of the translation is a bit different. My apologies. That's where it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, sir, here we see that it says "discussion and briefing along the lines of work" and then "Goran Macar." Can you tell us what this relates to and who Goran Macar was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the centre, security centre, we did not have the adequate personnel in order to process all those individuals that we had arrested in that operation. I believe that we sent a dispatch, or perhaps Mr. Kljajic agreed on the -- in a telephone conversation with the minister, that Mr. Goran Macar should come to the security centre, at the time he was the chief of the crime administration, and that he should bring with him five to ten crime police inspectors so that we would speed up this whole process and document all of the activities that Mr. Zuco was involved in, and to cap this with issuing crime reports, which is what it was called at the time, and sending them to the prosecutor. Here we also discussed some matters that were something that we were concerned with at the time. We had confiscated a number of vehicles. One of the issues that was discussed was where those vehicles were. And then there was also -- there were also some goods that were confiscated, and we wanted to do a report listing all the things that were confiscated in order to make sure that they were not abused.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown page 24. On the top of the page we see it says page 109. And the ERN number is 0605-4599. I'm sorry, I really don't know what English translation page would be the appropriate page. I hope that we can, with the assistance of the Usher or Registrar, have it. That's the page preceding the entry for the 10th of August. So just a page before this, please. Toward the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us what this means here. It says "Janja manning levels up to 30," and then it says "dismiss pensioners or retirees." Now, first of all, tell us what Janja is and what this bullet point refers to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Janja was a settlement not far from Bijeljina, some 10 kilometres away, and at the time, the place was predominantly Muslim and those Muslims had remained in the area at the time that we are talking about, and because all around it were Serbian villages and Serbian police and military forces, it was our assessment at one point that we should reinforce or become -- that we should have a visible police presence in the area in order to prevent attacks on some of these families, the Muslim families there, because there were such instances where they were assaulted, and to prevent possible assaults on them, or looting or murders, and based pursuant to this assessment of ours and in view of the fact that there was a small police department in Janja at the time, we actually upgraded it to a police station in order to enable it to function normally, because in peacetime it had some six to seven police officers, but once there were ten police officers or above, then that would be a higher level police station or presence. So based on our assessment, we decided that we had to strengthen this police department in Janja and have more police officers there, and thus we would automatically upgrade this police department to a police station. So we decided here to add additional 30 police officers to the Janja Police, and we had the capability to do so because there were people who had moved into our area from other parts. And in view of the fact that there were a number of retired police officers who were still working in Janja at the police station and they had at the time already been over 60 years of age, we decided to retire them and to place them, to move them, to the reserve force because I believe at the time under the law that would -- they would be qualified for reserve forces up to 65 and to replace them with younger police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, all this activity in Janja -- well, first of all, could you tell us whether this police station in Janja set up check-points on the approaches to Janja village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was only one road leading from Bijeljina to Zvornik and Pale and that road went through Janja. We set up check-points there and our objective was to do what we had already done in Bijeljina municipality at large, in other words, to prevent looting and to guarantee personal security and the personal safety and security of the property that belonged to the Muslims who lived in Janja at the time. We set up those check-points, and I believe we even established an intervention platoon that was -- that had its seat on the premises of the police station in Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What was the role of the intervention platoon? What was their basic purpose? Why were they in their police station in Janja?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we look at this time, you can see it if you analyse it, but at the time when we strengthened the police station in Janja, we did not have any cases of looting or persecutions or any other type of crimes, so we were trying to provide for normal conditions for these people to live in, because these people were farmers at the time. I think that was basically the structure of the population in Janja. And even to this day they are farmers. So we wanted to allow them to be -- to make it possible for them to go to their fields and do their work, do their farming, and to have normal living conditions in the environment and under the conditions that existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us take look at the entry on page 26, dated 11 August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on the following page at the bottom in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, here's an entry dated 11 August 1992, "Discussion on further activities," and then some places are listed. Could you please tell us, we can see that Ugljevik and Lopare are mentioned, has this anything to do with what you were saying on Friday? Do comment, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We acquainted the number one man of the crime police with all the problems we were facing at the time, and here it is stated that in the coming period we should continue the same kind of activities that we had taken in Brcko and Zvornik in Ugljevik and Lopare, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next entry is 12 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose it must be on the following page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 13 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is 13 August 1992, and it says "discussion with the president of Zvornik municipality." "Zvornik SJB - urgently resolve personnel issues," and so on. Please comment so that I needn't read it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The internal personnel structure of the MUP had been changed, and we had to conduct manning with appropriate personnel and thus stabilize the situation inside the MUP. On 13 August we scheduled a meeting with the president of Zvornik municipality. We, of course, informed him of the activities that we had in Zvornik at the time and presented our current problems to him, the internal problems of the ministry, but of course it was up to us to resolve them. As far as I can tell from my entry, we were somewhat dissatisfied with the co-operation with the VRS. The co-operation was not as it should be. At some difficult moments there was no information exchange. And as the largest organisation and the strongest force at the time, they were present there, but there wasn't much information exchange. So we requested that a different approach be taken to this problem and that we should tackle these piled up problems together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the very end of this page I can see a bullet point reading, "Ostoja Minic for chief of the crime service in Zvornik." Who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember who exactly he is. He may have come from Tuzla or Kalesija or some other nearby place. We thought that this man should take over the position of the chief of the crime service in Zvornik, and that's probably why he was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's show page 33 to the witness, please. It is not dated. ERN is 0605-4617. We can see that the last date mentioned before this entry is 13 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Foca is mentioned. Can you explain? Let us just wait to get the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose it must be on the following page. No, it must be the one after this. Yes, toward the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said already, while we were briefing Mr. Stanisic about the activities in Zvornik, the same roughly applies to our trip to Foca. Before making this entry, I was invited by Mr. Stanisic to come to Bosanska Vila. I think he was in Belgrade officially. And as far as I remember, he told me that he had received a dispatch or a report from Foca that paramilitaries there are disrupting the functioning of government and that they oppose all decisions taken by the legal authorities, that the situation was basically the same as in the Semberija municipalities. They are trying to meddle with the manning of the police station in Foca and also to influence other government structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 22, line 9, it has been recorded that Mr. Stanisic was in Belgrade officially, but I believe that you said something else too. Did you know that Mr. Stanisic was in Belgrade officially, or on a private visit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. He was probably there in an official capacity because he invited me to come. If he had been on a private visit, he would probably have invited me to meet him in a pub or something. But the way it was, it points more toward an official trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is 30 men. The group or unit that was supposed to go to Foca was meant to be 30 strong or --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that reference is made here to 30 uniformed police members. And the team that was meant to go to Foca should have been -- should have comprised also some crime police officers, a man named Milorad Orasanin. And I believe, although I'm not certain, that a member of state security should have come with us, and I think his name is Goran Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at page 36. It says "draft dispatches for the MUP of Serbia and that of Crna Gora." Can you explain what this was about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a logical sequence of events. There were two republics of the then state - I'm not sure what it was called at that moment, Yugoslavia or Serbian Montenegro - and we had to contact their MUPs because that was the only way that we could get to Foca, because the BH Army still controlled Trnovo and Gorazde, too. I think I informed the minister that a dispatch should be sent to the MUP of Serbia and the MUP of Montenegro to allow us free passage through their territories. I think that we planned to go via Pljevlja and Cajnice to Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Andan, what assignment did the minister give you and that unit that was going to Foca? What were you supposed to do there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to smile, but I can only repeat what he had said: This must be done at any cost. The paramilitaries in Foca must be wiped out. We must exercise all our legal powers, and that includes the use of fire-arms if the legal conditions are met. To enable the legitimate authorities in Foca to function. To process all members of paramilitary units, especially one Pedo, or Pedolino. I still remember their nicknames. They were local criminals who were behind all the trouble in Foca. Our goal was to disarm them and detain them, to search their premises, and every paramilitary formation had a warehouse where they stored their booty. It was our task to process all this and to go through the procedure all the way to the public prosecutor's office. We were also supposed to stay in Foca and assist the authorities and the Foca Police Station for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And since I'm moving to another -- another issue, I would ask that we are adjourned at this moment. But before that, I would offer this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Does that mean you're through with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment, return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andan, did you take part in the Zvornik operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer this question, I have to ask the Trial Chamber and those who are responsible for the air conditioning in this room that we are in, if you want me to finish my testimony here and if you want me to remain in good health and able to do so, could you please regulate the temperature in this room? I directly took part in the operation. Oh, yes, and what I'm asking for is that you turn this off. This amount of air conditioning in this room is really ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you're saying that it is too hot in here, is that correct, and you want the temperature to be lowered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, on the contrary. It is pleasant in the courtroom, but this other room that I'm in, it's like a refrigerator. I mean, during the breaks, the room that I'm in during the breaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. We will see to that. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood your question correctly, you asked me whether I took part in the operation of eliminating the paramilitaries, the Yellow Wasps. Yes, most directly. I don't know whether it is something to brag about or not, but I am the one who directly arrested Vukovic, nicknamed Zuco.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Vuckovic, Vojin, nicknamed Zuco; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Since his nickname was Zuco, the unit was called "Zute Ose," the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, briefly though, how you arrested him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of all the intelligence that we had available, during the early morning hours we took all the buildings that were being used by all these paramilitary units. We arrested the persons there. As for their personal weapons and everything else, we took all of that with us. We left the police on the spot to guard the premises so that the scene could be dealt with properly. When we started identifying the persons involved, carrying out the triage, as it is called, Vojin Vuckovic was not among them. And Rade Tanaskovic wasn't either. He was another one of the key persons from Zuco's paramilitary unit. In the meantime, we received information that the commander of the police station, a certain Maric, was in direct contact with Zuco throughout, and at that point in time he was at the Zvornik Police Station. We put a bit of pressure on him to tell us where Zuco is. And he said that Zuco was in Celopek near Zvornik, in the house of Rade Tanaskovic. As we were preparing for the arrest, it crossed my mind that we should take the commander of the police station to Celopek, which is indeed what we did. I said to him -- once we had surrounded the house where the mentioned persons were, I said to him that he should knock at the door, and when somebody on the other side says who it is, then he should introduce himself and say that he urgently needs to see Vojin Vuckovic, Zuco. That's exactly what we did. When the door was being unlocked, he stood on the side. The door was unlocked by Zuco. He was wearing shorts. He had a pistol. We reacted at lightening speed. We took his pistol. I don't want it to seem that we had done this mildly. There was quite a fight involved, fists and the like. Perhaps that's not appropriate altogether, that's what we did and that was the end of that. Once we were done, another man walked out of another room, again he was in his underwear too. We identified him as Rade Tanaskovic, and we took them to the police station and handed them over to the crime investigation service for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, just when was this exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when this happened? Can you remember exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same day when we entered Zvornik and when we eliminated most of the paramilitaries, Zuco's paramilitaries. I think that we eliminated them by 6.00 in the morning, and then between 6.00 and 7.00 on that same date - I don't remember the exact date - we dealt with Vojin Vuckovic and Rade Tanaskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: On which date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know it was sometime in August. I've already told you, do forgive me, I'm not good at dates. And in these notes of mine, it should say what date it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, these persons who were arrested at the time, were they remanded in custody for 72 hours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, may I also say that because we were not able to work properly in Zvornik, these persons were taken to the CSB Bijeljina by bus under police escort, and then in Bijeljina we dealt with them individually. Of course, all of these persons were issued with appropriate papers certifying the fact that they were remanded in custody. So all of this was dealt with lawfully, that's what I'm saying. So they were given a decision on detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P317.18. That is tab 74. Could we please have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a decision on detention, Milivojevic, Slobodan, nicknamed Topola. It is signed by SJB chief Dragan Andan. And then further on in documents 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 pages and then the last one, page 8, there is a decision on detention concerning Vojin Vuckovic, nicknamed Zuco. Are those the decisions that you were thinking of when you were giving your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature. These were the decisions that were written up by the crime investigation service. I just confirmed that these were the persons involved with my own signature, and a seal was affixed, and, of course, they were remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 19D1. Can we have a look at that, please. That is tab 83 of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 31st of July, 1992, and there is a signature there. Can you tell us whose signature this is and whose report this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise because I didn't know the date earlier on. This document shows that the operation was implemented on the 29th and 30th of July. In response to your question, I said I think the beginning of August. I do apologise once again. I see now that it was actually the 29th and 30th of July, and Zuco was arrested on the same day, the 29th. This is my signature, and this is a brief description of what happened. And we probably sent this to the Ministry of the Interior to inform them in brief terms what it was that we had done and to what extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like it to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My microphone is on now. I don't know if they hear me now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Yes, we do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could you please have a look at 65 ter 166D1, tab 87. Your Honours, just one small intervention in relation to the previous document, 1D558, that was admitted a moment ago. I have just been informed by my colleague Ms. Savic that an identical document, unsigned, was introduced as P1557.11 and admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to this document. That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was waiting for you to, having informed us of that, and? Is the idea that this -- the signed one be substituted for the exhibit that's already with us? Or is this a supplement? I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, I just wanted to relate these two documents for the benefit of the Trial Chamber because they are different, since this document which was now admitted as 1D558 was signed by the witness and witness confirmed that. However, the other document which is identical has no signature and it was admitted as a P document, so that was the only reason I raise this. But it's up to Mr. Hannis if he wants to intervene on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only wanted to indicate that the other document, the unsigned version, was part of the 92 ter package of a witness, and therefore it was a document that was originally introduced in the Krajisnik trial several years ago. So that was a version we had that didn't have a signature. But because it was referred to, I think by that witness, I would like to leave that number in evidence. We now have on the record the linking between those two, and I think that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Sir, could we please have on our screens 65 ter 166D1, tab 87. This is not the document. Yes, now we have it before us. Tab 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a dispatch dated August 1st, 1992. The document is signed or, rather, it is typed "Chief Dragan Andan," his signature is typed out, and in the penultimate sentence towards the end, it says: "The operation to mop up Zvornik is yielding positive results with regard to the security and general situation in Zvornik." Could you please comment on this. First of all, could you tell us whether this is indeed your dispatch, whether you're familiar with it, and could you then briefly comment on the portion that I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my dispatch, although I have to say that to this day I am not clear why we informed the ministry about our operations, because every time we would have to go to the ministry to receive information from them and then send reports. I asked Mr. Gajic and he just sort of waved with his hand away, you know, like saying that's how we were ordered to do. And I can only say that you may find a number of dispatches of this type. And in the penultimate sentence, I'm actually reporting that we had practically completed this operation of wiping out these and actually expelling them from the Zvornik municipality, these paramilitaries, and we wanted to let them know that the situation, the security situation, was now very good and that we will continue to do our jobs that were, under the law, what we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 31 in line 8, it says "I asked Mr. Gajic."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Cedo Gajic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, could you please tell us exactly the name, the first and last names, slowly and then what his function was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was undersecretary for public security, Cedo Kljajic, who was at the time with us in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objection, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D559, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I would like to show you is under tab 84. The document is marked as 65 ter 164D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is another dispatch. It is dated the 31st of July, 1992, and it was sent to the Serbian MUP, and again we see that it was signed by Chief Dragan Andan, or, rather, that name was typed out. And this dispatch is about the Vlasenica-Zvornik road and it discusses the members of paramilitary units in the Zvornik area. Could you just tell us, please, could you comment briefly on this document with regard to these two matters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to explain, since I see that you have the original dispatch, I would like to explain why the signature is missing. There is no signature because at the time we did it this way: The typist would type out the dispatch, I would sign it, but then the dispatch would have to be encoded, and then of course there could be no signature appearing there. In other words, the dispatch would be sent on -- it would be sent encoded to the addressees, whereas the original with my signature on would remain, would be kept on files. Now, this road mentioned here, the Vlasenica-Zvornik, led over a hill and then it went through Sehovici, Vlasenica, that part of Mount Romanija, towards Sarajevo. On several occasions, at least at the time when I was in Bijeljina, members of the BH Army carried out sabotage activities, and they cut off the roads, they opened fire on soldiers and vehicles, and there is mention made here of one of such incidents. The other matter that you mentioned, as far as I could see here, was that we said we were undertaking intensive activities to process the individuals who had been committed -- who had been arrested and that we would probably in the near future embark on legal proceedings. This was the course of action that we did and that we took when we arrested these people, these individuals, during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you just answer this question: On this road, the only road that you said which connected Zvornik and Sarajevo and which ran through Sehovici, Vlasenica, and Caparde, is Crni Vrh also on this road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D560, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, the Court just has one question relating to the last document, 1D560. If we could have it back on the screen. Because we were not quite sure about who exactly is referred to in the document. The last paragraph reads that: "Intensive activities are underway to process individuals who have committed crimes and members of paramilitary formations in the Zvornik area." And this is dated the 31st of July. Are we right to understand that the members of the paramilitary formations to whom you are referring in this dispatch were paramilitary formations such as the Yellow Wasps, or is it Muslim paramilitary formations? You see, Mr. Andan, we were not quite sure of who exactly was it who closed the road between Vlasenica and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, obviously I was talking about two separate matters. Here we report that we were taking a criminal action against the Zute Ose paramilitary unit, and in the meantime, the traffic on the road was interrupted because members of the BH Army had carried out a sabotage unit and cut off this only road leading to Sarajevo. So these are two completely separate matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. It's clear to us now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D75, tab 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report or information entitled "information on MUP activities on exposing the criminal activities of paramilitary formation Zute ose in the area of Serb municipality of Zvornik." And the number is 02-16/92. It is dated the 4th of August, 1992. And on page 3 there is no signature. We can only see the date. It says Bijeljina, the 4th of August, 1992. Are you familiar with this report or information and could you tell us who authored it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this information. It was drafted by members of the crime department. And there is no signature because this is just an information. And a document is missing here, the cover letter, where probably either I or somebody else on my behalf signed that cover letter and forwarded it to the Ministry of the Interior. The normal procedure was not to sign the information but to sign the cover letter that is sent to an institution or to a person, whichever the case may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in the last paragraph of this information on page 3, there is mention of what the Serb police learned and members of national security operatives and that was that a Dusan Vuckovic, aka Repic, committed a massacre genocide over citizens of the Serb Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina of the Muslim ethnicity. And then it goes on to say verification and materialisation of this information was being taken care of by the Serb armed forces, military police, in co-operation with MUP national security operatives. Mr. Andan, do you recall, as stated here, that you had information to this effect at the time, and do you recall that this problem was dealt with by the military police and state security operatives or national security operatives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we gathered intelligence, and through intelligence we learned that Vojin Vuckovic executed Muslims for gain, personal gain, and there was a time when he executed people only because they were of Muslim ethnicity, and I believe that I informed the chief of national security at the time, Goran Zukic, of this, that he confirmed the information that I had received and told me that they were already conducting a police investigation into these events involving Repic. When Repic was arrested, this whole process was finalised. And as far as I can recall, after Repic was processed he was handed over to military security organs in Bijeljina, and a little later I believe that he was indicted and tried, I believe in Sabac, for the crimes that he had committed in Zvornik municipality. I even learned that he was evaluated, his mental state was evaluated, and that he was declared mentally unstable, but to what extent, I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could we just go back to the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document number, let me repeat that, is 02-16/92, dated the 4th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown P1557.12. That's under tab 108. 108.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, perhaps I've skipped it, but I can't see 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you please take a look at the screen. My apologies. It's there. Sir, this document, bearing number 02-16/92 dated the 4th of August, 1992, and we see that it is signed by approval or with the approval of the minister by Goran Macar, and it says: "We are hereby submitting as an attachment a report on the activities of the MUP to detect the criminal activities of Zute Ose, Yellow Wasps, paramilitary unit on the territory of Zvornik Serb municipality." And it was sent to the minister at Pale. Is this the cover letter that you mentioned a little earlier, the cover letter that was missing from that report and which explains why that report or that information was unsigned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in general this cover letter would actually be the first page of the entire package sent to the ministry. I told you a moment ago that I wasn't sure whether it was me who had signed this or somebody else, but here we see it and it shows that it was on the way we normally did things, according to standard procedure, and especially so because we see here that it says that "we are hereby submitting as an attachment a report," and then as under attachments it lists that there are 65 statements attached to the information as well, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's show the witness 65 ter 363D1. That's tab 126. I apologise, I have just seen something. Could we go back to the previous document, P1557, to comment on it before we continue. I do apologise. The English text is all right. Could we just display the Serbian again, P1557.12.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you mention among the attachments a photocopy of a certificate by Pale SJB, do you know who chief of the Pale SJB was at the time? And I'm referring to the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was still Malko Koroman. There were still some problems with him, but I don't know if that's relevant here. And if you wish, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of the case when the minister of the interior of the RS tried to remove Malko Koroman from his position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you phrased it adequately. He tried to remove him. There was information, at least that's what I heard, that he had abused his official position, that he had links with crime, and that Mr. Stanisic in writing demanded that he be replaced and that the police station at Pale be handed over to somebody else. In 1992, I forget which month it was, the authorised officials from the administration came to perform the take-over. Over 3.000 armed persons had gathered. They were armed with long-barrelled weapons. And as far as I know, they drove out those authorised officials and drafted an appeal to -- or a petition to President Karadzic for Malko Koroman to remain in his position. And as far as I know, he did. And sometime later, a month, two, or three, I don't know, a compromise solution was found, and he was appointed to the position of chief inspector of the RS, and he went to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Chief inspector of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Looking at the English transcript, I wonder if counsel could clarify what's at line 12. It doesn't seem to make sense in English the way it's translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, on that occasion when those 3.000 armed men came to Pale or, rather, gathered there, was it then that pursuant to Karadzic's intervention Malko Koroman remained chief of the Pale SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Malko Koroman eventually replaced from the position of chief of Pale SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. And he was transferred to another position in the -- in the police administration. He became chief inspector of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then he was transferred to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that the ministry headquarters was in Bijeljina for a while. I had already left the ministry when its headquarters was in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us return to the document that I wanted to show you already. 65 ter 363D1, tab 126. This is a letter to the Department for Prevention and Detection of General Crime of the Zvornik SJB. We see your name in the signature block and your signature as well. Tell us what this document is about. It says, in the subject line, "submission of objects from the Yellow Wasps operation."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Yellow Wasps were arrested, we also arrested two Simic brothers. One of them was a owner of a jewellery shop before the war and we suspected him of buying gold from those paramilitaries. There was intelligence that his wife was in Banja Koviljaca in Serbia, and we requested the Serbian MUP to search their family house in Banja Koviljaca in co-operation with the local MUP authorities. We confiscated 2.2 kilograms of gold on that occasion. We also confiscated a BMW automobile owned by him. And we initiated a verification process regarding the provenance of that gold. Mr. Simic was able to prove that he was the rightful owner of that gold, which he had obtained legally. And then we returned those 2.2 kilograms of gold jewellery and the automobile to him. This letter shows who handed over and who received these items, and I signed this document, which is not a dispatch. But the crime prevention services is ordered to summon Simic and return these items to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We can read here in the second paragraph: "Since most of these people reside in your area, you need to return their personal belongings to them." Does this letter therefore relate only to Simic or to other persons as well from whom the Yellow Wasps had taken some property which is now being returned as a result of the Yellow Wasps operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two-thirds or even more of the members of that unit were from the Zvornik municipality, and the investigation -- and the investigation couldn't be established that the property was mostly illegally gained, so --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the end of his answer. The interpreter didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The latter part of your answer was not recorded. Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, briefly, I said that two-thirds of these persons were from the Zvornik municipality. The investigation established that the objects found with them were not gained by criminal offences, and we ordered the crime prevention service to return these items to the persons concerned because they are no longer subject to criminal processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D561, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P341, which is tab 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, do you remember if after the arrest of the Yellow Wasps the chief of the Zvornik SJB was replaced?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the consent of the undersecretary and probably that of the minister, we replaced all executives at the Zvornik SJB because in our opinion they had not lived up to their responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 161D1, please, which is tab 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document signed by the newly appointed chief of the Zvornik SJB, Locancevic [phoen]. It was sent to the MUP, the crime prevention and combatting service, and the Bijeljina CSB. I'm interested in item 2 on page 1. It says information about illegal activities and the legal affairs department of the public security station. Did you know about this and did you establish during the Zvornik operation that there had been irregularities there and what did they consist of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but what we see on the screen is not what you are talking about. This is probably a technical shortcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Let us first display the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 141D1, tab 121. The document is dated 11 August 1992. We are interested in page 2 of the English translation. More specifically item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have a hard copy in your binder, sir. I believe that it's more easily legible. Do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know of this incident. Mr. Lazic was chief of the administration and legal affairs section of the Zvornik SJB. During our investigation, we established that Vojin Vuckovic, also known as Zuco, through Lazic, if only temporarily, was able to legalise stolen cars by getting traffic permits from Lazic, and Zuco then transferred them to Serbia and sold them there. I believe that the investigation showed that he also issued some documents by which he committed a criminal offence, and we suspended the man and temporarily removed him from the MUP. And in accordance with the law, we filed a criminal complaint against Mr. Lazic to the public prosecutor's office in Bijeljina or Zvornik, I'm not sure about the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D562, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the Zute Osa or Yellow Wasps case ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At least that aspect ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So my question is, these Yellow Wasps that were processed by the crime prevention and detection service, were they covered by a criminal complaint submitted to the public prosecutor's office in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was our duty then, in addition to the criminal report with the description of the crime involved, to provide all the evidence that we had gathered during our operations, so all of this was properly handed over to the public prosecutor's office in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After a while were they released from custody on the basis of a decision made by the prosecutor and the investigating judge of the court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes. Once they were released, some other problems came to the fore, and we are probably going to discuss that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead. What were these problems on account of their release?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because of their release, the family house of Mico Davidovic was monitored, also the house where I was staying temporarily, and also the observation of some other persons who were direct participants in that operation of ours, that is to say, the top personnel involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "observation," tell me, what do you mean? An observation by who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This problem was particularly pronounced in relation to myself, because parts of this paramilitary unit, even Zuco himself, from time to time came close to the building where I was, and the information we had indicated that shortly they would try not only to kill me, but also Mico Davidovic and all the other key people who were involved in the operation of their arrest at the time. As I said, this was particularly pronounced in relation to myself because I will explain later how it was that I left the ministry and I was therefore without any support and any protection. As a matter of fact, I think that some persons, some individuals from Bijeljina whom I had also arrested and detained, instigated Mr. Vukcevic [phoen] to commit something that abominable, that is to say, assassinate me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, you and other persons you mentioned here who were threatened by the members of this paramilitary unit that had been set free, or, rather, they were provisionally released, were you concerned about your own safety and the safety of your family members who lived with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was concerned, primarily for my family members. I had two children who were under age at the time, two sons. Then my wife was there, too, as well. And I was the only one who could protect them. I had no other protection and I was worried. I was so worried that once I called Mr. Davidovic in Belgrade and I said to him, because Davidovic's unit had already withdrawn from Bijeljina, I said to him that I had some information, what I already told this Court about, and that quite simply I was afraid to spend nights by the window with a cocked rifle in the fear of having my house being attacked. He sent two young men who were guarding my house for about ten days and in that way both my family and myself felt a bit less encumbered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, you said that you were concerned, worried, and that that is why you spent the nights by the window with a cocked rifle without any lights on; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. Because I can see better if the light is not on in the room where I'm sitting, because that was particularly the case during the night, when they would circle around the house either on foot or in cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Trial Chamber, the exhibits that deal with this question are P317.21, and P344, P637, P345, and P195. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could we have tab numbers for those documents? That would be ...
