utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honours. Tabs 140, 142, 143, 144, and 149.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 22P1. That is 118A; that's the tab number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a dispatch of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, Sarajevo. It is signed by the minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic. In this dispatch instructions are provided as follows: "In accordance with the decision of the Presidency, the MUP and the Ministry of Justice should obtain officially correct information in relation to the behaviour of the Serb authorities in terms of the treatment of war prisoners and the conditions of life of detainees in prisons in the municipalities where there are such cases. All public security stations are duty-bound to act in accordance with the decision of the Presidency." Instructions are provided here about the freedom of movement and so on. We have the entire order. It says that with regard to the measures taken and the situation as it is, you are duty-bound to inform this information by the 14th of August, 1992. Do you remember having received this kind of dispatch in the beginning of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, did you act in accordance with this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That is our duty by law, and we responded in an appropriate manner. In the area of Bijeljina, we did not have any detention centres or camps that were held by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 175D1, tab 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to have a look at that document. Sir, this is a document from the 11th of August, 1992. It is sent to the Eastern Bosnia Corps, and it's for the commander. It has to do with this dispatch. Actually, this dispatch that we looked at a moment ago is being sent to them. Can you give us your comment with regard to this document, because it says down here "Chief Dragan Andan," and somebody's signature is there as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody obviously signed this on my behalf, but this is an authentic dispatch, and this is accurate. In view of the subject matter, that it was treated by the dispatch that we received from the Ministry of the Interior, we did not have any information and there weren't any detention camps or detention centres for non-Serbs. Since we knew that the Batkovici camp was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska or, rather, of the Eastern Bosnia Corps, we sent this dispatch to the commander because they were the persons who were actually supposed to respond in an appropriate manner to the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether you received an answer from the Eastern Bosnian Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no. However, that does not necessarily mean that they did not provide a direct response to the government or the Ministry of the Interior, but we did not receive any answer from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document also be admitted into evidence, please, if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objections. And did you want the earlier one as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the earlier one is already exhibited as the order by the ministry, but I will have to check over the break and I will inform you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But this document which, according to the witness, yielded no response, what does it add to what we already know? It's a request for information. There was no response. Why do we need it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but it clearly -- it clearly indicates the fact that the Ministry of the Interior in Bijeljina did not have anything to do with the Batkovici war camp and that it was under the specific and exclusive authority of the army, and therefore I think that for that reason this is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that's a further-reaching conclusion than I would say stems from it, but I think it is a contemporaneous writing by this witness which reflects his state of mind about the status of that camp and therefore I think it's relevant. It goes to the weight of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D563, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the break, to resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the break, at page 47, line 24 and -5, we were talking about the document which I showed to the witness immediately prior to the break. It's 65 ter 22D1 and our tab 118A. And Mr. Hannis was questioning whether this document will be exhibited, and I said that we will check, that I believe the document is already exhibited with a similar wording in it. And we have located the document. It bears the exhibit number P999. This is all the information that I wanted to give to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, before we go on, may I just ask whether the air conditioning situation has been regulated or do you still have a problem?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's been regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 653 -- 653D1 is the 65 ter number. Tab 25. Tab 125.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, this is a document signed by the War Presidency of Brcko, Djordje Ristanic, sent on the 12th of August, 1992, to the CSB Bijeljina and the corps command. And in paragraph 2 it says that it's the "decision of the War Presidency to issue an order banning the population from leaving our municipality without special approval from the military command in case of military personnel or approval from the Brcko Public Security Station in the case of the rest of the population." As far as we can see, it has do with the problem referred to in the first paragraph, that they have problems with soldiers and other military conscripts who leave military obligation and compulsory work service without authorisation, so they say return them or arrest them. Can you give us your comment on this document and in your view which population does this document refer to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertains to the Serb population, military age, able-bodied men who for a variety of reasons were fleeing from the front line and thereby destabilising the line. This order is, of course, addressed to the security centre. I think that in accordance with legal regulations that were in force we did not have the ability to arrest people, that was in accordance with the law. However, we would send them to the public security station and then they would send them to the military security, so that is how the cycle went. It refers to ethnic Serbs, military age, who were fleeing from the front line, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you base that conclusion on, that these are ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it was addressed to us and the military security and since special approvals were required for leaving the combat area, I assert that these are ethnic Serbs who either due to the pressure of paramilitary formations or due to fear or Serb heroism when you drink a litre or two, I don't know, but at any rate this pertains to ethnic Serbs of military age.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, do you have any knowledge to the effect that such problems that had to do with the fact that persons who had a military obligation to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska -- actually, were such cases frequent? Did people often leave units of their own free will and did they flee from their obligations, as it were, in the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This problem did not exist only in the area of the municipality of Brcko. This problem pertained to a great many municipalities, especially those that were bordering with the Republic of Serbia, so mobilisation could not fully be carried out, the one that was in force at the time. I had a few other examples of people who we arrested and took to the front line. That was just the way the times were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What do you wish to show, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness can take the ... Your Honours, the allegations throughout the case were that the police had the role in establishing the places on the roads where they were checking and maltreating the non-Serb population, checking their identity papers and so on and so forth. Now, this document shows that the reason why these places were established in the first place was essentially for the reasons because the Serbs were fleeing their obligation to participate in the mobilisation and the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, that is the purpose of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the Chamber, Judge Harhoff dissenting, agrees that it should be admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, when -- before the witness was brought in, I was referring to the document which has already been exhibited as P999. Now I'm informed that this document is MFI'd. Now, as the witness acknowledges the receipt of this -- of the document which I showed him, which is essentially the very same document, I propose, if Mr. Hannis does not object, and I hope he will not, that the document P999 be de-MFI'd at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not opposed to de-MFI'ing the Prosecution exhibit, but I would like to indicate on the record I would like to leave open my option, perhaps, to move in the Defence exhibit upon examination if I see they're not precisely identical and there's some reason that I would want to do that. But for now I'm content to have P999 become a full exhibit without the MFI designator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It was marked for identification pending what?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't recall. I assume that was Defence objection at the time because we didn't have a witness who was familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, we are checking what is the situation. We just had the information that it was P999 MFI. That is why I brought it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But Mr. Hannis having indicated his - reservation is too strong a word - his caveat, I suppose, we would de-MFI it. One of these days I'm going to come up with a phrase with which I'm comfortable, but for the moment I go along with the convention of "de-MFI'ing" it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We are informed by the Court Officer that it was only marked for identification because it was not on the 65 ter list. Thank you, Anna.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, therefore we withdraw our objection in that respect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir -- P410 MFI'd. Could that document please be shown to you. That is tab 71.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document that does not bear a date. On the last page we just see July 1992, and we see Danilo Vukovic chief, by way of a signature, and on the first page we see that this is a report on the results of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- in SJB Bijeljina for the period from the 26th of June until the 25th of July, 1992, as well as a summary of information on certain operative observations regarding criminal acts and other illegal acts in the period of war and immediate post-war events in Bijeljina. Sir, my first question: Was Danilo Vukovic head of the department for crime prevention and crime investigation in the SJB Bijeljina in the relevant period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this report? Obviously it's a monthly report, it includes a 30-day period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who was this report sent to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report had to be sent to the appropriate departments, namely the crime police department, the uniformed police department, the analysis people, and quite often such a report is sent to the Minister of the Interior. It is not compulsory, but it happened not very seldom that such reports were sent to the minister as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, there is no doubt -- or, rather, is it beyond any doubt that this report was sent to the ministry headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was sent to the ministry headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. I would like to ask that it be de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to that promotion, elevation, or whatever term we would like to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we remove the MFI classification or qualification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more intervention in the transcript: 53/21, I think that this is a continuation of the witness's answer rather than my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember your answer when I asked you about this report. You were explaining - you were explaining - who these reports were usually sent to, which departments; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 53/21 should be part of the witness's answer. 65 ter 139D1. Tab 64. Could that document please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is entitled: "List of criminal reports submitted in the period from the 26th of June to the 25th of July, 1992, which we have not reported to you in dispatches owing to the interruption of dispatch communications." Tell me, since it involves the same time-period, is this report perhaps part of the previous document that we saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, are you familiar with this report, with this list, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. The more so because I was the one who insisted that such a run-down be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says here in the title that it is a list of complaints that had not been reported by way of dispatch because of an interruption in dispatch communications. Could you please clarify that or explain it a bit to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, as I have already said earlier, it was frequently the case that the dispatch or phone lines were down so that we had -- so that we sent all urgent information by courier. Obviously this was not a matter of any urgency, so that we sent it on a monthly basis. We compiled a list of criminal complaints and forwarded it to the Ministry of the Interior. And of course because of the subject matter, this kind of communication would also be sent to the analysis department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So have I understood your words correctly: This is an additional report with some additional criminal complaints that the ministry had not been informed of earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does this document pertain to all crimes that had been processed, as it were, or those that the police was aware of at the moment, that they had been committed, and where criminal complaints had been forwarded to the appropriate prosecutor at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the time-frame in question, and this report relates to that time-period and all those complaints that had been sent to the prosecutor at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D565, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 1D97. That's under tab 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document, or, rather, the cover letter attached to this document, bears your signature as the head of -- or chief of the Security Services Centre. It is dated the 29th of July, 1992, and it is addressed to the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Radovan Karadzic. Do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 it says that this is a report on the involvement and activities of the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in establishing authority under rule of law in the area covered by the Bijeljina Security Services Centre. And on the last page, page number 5, although it's probably page 4, or perhaps a page is missing from this document, we see again your signature there. Is that your signature and the date indicated there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in the paragraph before last, where, toward the end, it says: "In order to provide the full information, we have to stress that there were instances where members of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we encounter severe opposition among them and resistance, not only verbal but also armed," and then mention is made of three unsuccessful assaults on the premises of the CSB, on the building itself, could you please comment on this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is basically just a description of everything that we worked on and everything that we had to deal with at the time in Bijeljina. Earlier on I had already mentioned how there was a lot of disaffection because of the people of Serb ethnicity who were avoiding to be recruited and then they were sort of employed by the police stations. And then there was disaffection because of the curfew that was established. The local authorities wanted to control the work of the Ministry of the Interior, and we opposed that. And there were even individuals who went so far as to claim that we were the ones who were supposed to believe the Bijeljina area and just leave the paramilitary units there. So I will not talk about the political climate there; I will just talk about the security aspect. And I have to say that both citizens and security services employees were in jeopardy and it was my goal to try one more time to inform the highest, the top leadership of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina about the situation in Bijeljina and Majevica. Now, the second thing was, and you will -- I have to stress something about myself, I am an impatient person by nature and I don't like to leave things for tomorrow if they can be done today, so I was never happy with the fact that there were some paramilitary units entering the Republic of Republika Srpska and I deliberately addressed both the president of the government and the municipal political authorities, and this was an attempt to inform the highest leadership of the then leadership of Republika Srpska to inform them in detail of the security situation because -- and asking for their full support because we again had a situation where there was a new attempt to destabilise the situation in Bijeljina. There was Mauzer who appeared there and then others after him, and we were beginning to lose -- we were beginning to have a lot of loose ends and there were attempts to incite people against -- to opposing our orders and so on. So our purpose was to inform the highest leadership of the security situation in Bijeljina, trying in that way to obtain their political support for what measures we were trying to implement at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this document, we see on the last page that there is something in handwriting added on. Could you please just tell us that what that refers to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously this information did reach the then president of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic, and from what it says there, I see that he did support us, and I mean in terms of what we laid out in this letter, and he says that we should continue enforcing order and the rule of law in this area. I don't know if he meant other areas as well, but specifically he did mean Semberija and Majevica areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what Mrs. Biljana Plavsic's position was on -- and what her attitude was, what her take was, on paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I do know some of what her attitude or position was, and I know that there was even a written report relating to those matters. I don't know exactly where you could find it now, but it had to do with the release of Vojin Vuckovic, aka Zuco. He was released from prison, from Bijeljina. He went to Pale where he was seen by Mrs. Plavsic, that she made certain promises and gave certain promises to him. I don't know the details, but I do know that we sent information to that effect to the highest -- to Pale because she actually met with the leader of one of the cruelest paramilitary units. Now, we also handled this situation in a legal way, if I can put it that way. We learned, namely, that the certain Marko Pavlovic, who was the Chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence, having false personal documents issued in Sekovic. This Marko Pavlovic was supposed to be, and I think he was, from Backa Palanka. We surrendered this person, we handed him over to the national security organs, I believe he was taken to Pale. But after he was released, Mrs. Plavsic had a meeting with him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 165D1, tab 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report of the crime rate in the period between 1 July and 31 July 1992. Unfortunately we only have the first page of this document. Are you familiar with this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I'm also sorry that the remaining two or three pages are missing. This is not a TV commercial by any means, but we did try to act in accordance with the laws and regulations of the Republika Srpska at the time. And we made snap-shots of the situation. We never beefed up these reports. There was no need to. And we sent these reports to the ministry. And sometimes we would also copy the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm especially interested in the last two paragraphs of this document. Could you comment, if you remember what this is about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the last two?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know precisely now, but these people mentioned here as the perpetrators of murder had ties with Salko Kukic, and we say here that a criminal report was filed against them and that we took -- took all measures necessary against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the point is, is it the case that in both these cases the individuals involved are of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. And I have to say also that we filed criminal complaints against individuals of non-Serb ethnicities. I'm sure you can find it in our files. But we also submitted criminal reports against some Roma because they took advantage of the situation as it was then. They pretended they were Muslims and they went looting property, so in that way we tried also to prevent their activities and stop them from getting engaged in criminal activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you said that the members of Roma ethnicity actually declared themselves to be of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I said. They declared themselves to be of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, although this document is not complete and it was the best version we could obtain at this time, Your Honour, I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is -- have we had any further explanation about why it's incomplete or if the witness knows anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Witness, perhaps you can answer this question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I sit here, I don't know why it's incomplete, why two or three pages are missing. Because if there was page 1, obviously there should have been pages 2 and 3. Where they might be, I really don't know nor can I answer as I -- to that -- give an answer to that question as I sit here. But I can confirm that there was -- that this was a report from a period of one month where we reported on our work in that period. I cannot really explain why this is incomplete because I was just shown this report here and I hadn't seen it anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this is a satisfactory reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we're dealing with what we have, so I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I raise one other question: Can I ask about the provenance of this document? Is this an OTP document? Does it have an ERN?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm informed that this document was received from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: During proofing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, not during proofing. During probably one of the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have some further inquiry as to where he got it? Is it in his personal collection or was it received from another source?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Especially in light of his answer which appears at line 15 and 16 of the previous page: "I cannot really explain why this is incomplete because I was just shown this report here and I hadn't seen it anywhere else."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I may have received this document from Danilo Vukovic, or maybe I found it in the archives of the Ministry of the Interior, but as I said, I can't recall. There were two or three pages but I can't really ascertain here how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess, Your Honour, I'm going to object to it then. You heard his oral testimony about this, and I think that's adequate, given the lack of further information about the provenance, the document, and what and how much is missing and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I accept. So I withdraw my proposition to admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andan, I would like you to see now 1D392, tab 63. Sir, this document is dated 23rd of July, 1992. It's an authorisation issued to Dragan Andan. It is signed by the minister of the interior. And then we see that it says "for Mico Stanisic" because someone else signed it on his behalf. Do you recall receiving this authorisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Andan, I'd like to show you 65 ter 671D1. That's at tab 72A. When we looked at your diary, you told us about the meeting concerning your trip to Foca. This is a dispatch sent to the prime minister, Mr. Djeric, where he's informed that the security and political situation in Foca is critical and that on 23rd July there were significant, numerous incidents in the town itself in which members of the MUP were assaulted, disarmed, and beaten up and their property destroyed. And there is a request that certain responsible individuals headed by the prime minister should visit the town, come there in person to see the situation. Now, tell us, in the meeting that you had with the minister, were you told anything about these events here? Were you told anything about the situation in Foca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Minister Stanisic did tell me about what he knew about this, and he also related some additional information that was not entered in this dispatch, information based on intelligence that he had received from the security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any other reports on the situation in Foca, and if so, who from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right before my departure to Foca -- and let me also say that we didn't go to Foca because we didn't receive approval from the MUP of Serbia to pass through their territory with long-barrelled weapons. But I did get additional information from Mico Davidovic who had gone to Pljevlja with the same unit with which he was in Bijeljina, and there he disarmed a Chetnik formation. I believe that its leader was called Ceko or some such. And he also got intelligence from Foca there. And something I heard from him confirmed everything that we saw in this dispatch and more. And the other piece of information referred directly to me and the other persons that were supposed to go to Foca. Davidovic had learned that these persons knew that somebody would come from Bijeljina to disarm them and implement the legal procedure. They were going to ambush us outside of Foca and their primary goal was to kill me. I even think that Mr. Davidovic drafted a dispatch that he forwarded to the MUP containing this intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D566, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court's indulgence. 65 ter 24D1, can we show that, please. Tab 129.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document was sent to the public security station, and the signatory is the undersecretary of the public security station Cedo Kljajic. Probably there is something wrong with this. It was sent to the Zvornik SJB. Could you comment on this document, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, clearly the signature block is wrong. He can't be undersecretary of the public security station. He can be undersecretary for public security. We needed a minibus big enough to transport 30 police officers from Bijeljina to Foca. So this is a request to be given a vehicle to transport 30 uniformed personnel to Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us turn to page 3, but I believe that your page is wrongly marked. Do look at the screen. I'm not sure that you have the right page in your binder because I don't have one in mine. This was signed by Dragan Kijac, and it's dated 19 August 1992. Is this the document you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document was drafted to call a meeting at the Bijeljina SJB on the 20th of August to organise the departure to Foca. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And this meeting was indeed held. We also discussed some details that were important for this operation, and Mr. Radovic also played an important role because he had fresh information about the overall security information. He was supposed to come to Foca with us as the representative of national security.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now let me show you page 2 of the document. It's dated 19 August and in the signature block we read "Minister of the Interior Mico Stanisic." But it seems that somebody else signed on his behalf. And we see that the document was sent to the Serbian MUP and the Montenegro MUP. Can you comment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that we were unable to reach Foca unless we go through the territory of two other countries or republics. And these two are Serbia and Montenegro. Lest they should treat us as a paramilitary unit, and in order to legalise our passage through their territories, we sent this official dispatch to the two MUPs. And as far as I remember, the MUP of Montenegro never replied. And as far as I remember, the reply of the Serbian MUP was negative. The planned operation had to be put off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D567, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to show you document 65 ter 23D1, dated 10 August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which tab?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, we're done with this. We're moving on. Mr. Andan, I'm going to show you document 65 ter 15D1. That's tab 42. This is an Official Note dated 4 July 1992. And it says: "Pursuant to an order from Deputy Minister of the Serbian MUP Cedo Kljajic." It's about a poker machine. Can you tell us more about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. And I'm glad you raised this because I was afraid you wouldn't. This is an Official Note showing that I took a poker machine that was deposited at the SJB and used it for operative purposes. I can say to this Trial Chamber under oath what it was all about at the time. In the Jana municipality we found a person who we used as an informant. That person owned a small catering establishment, and I took this poker machine from our storage for this person to use as a -- to pay him back for what he had done to us. And this poker machine later turned into a Damocles sword above my head. I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on and then you can explain later. But let me ask you, is this document an official certificate that you took this poker machine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an official confirmation that I took this poker machine from our storage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you going to tender it? I have no objection if we could have some evidence from the witness about the signatures, if you he knows who either of those belong to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You heard the question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, that's my signature; and on the left-hand side, the signature of the warehouse manager. I don't remember who it was at the time. Mr. Marjanovic possibly. But certainly on the right-hand side these are my initials or my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the reaction of the Trial Chamber with regard to this document. I agree it is not directly relevant for this trial and this indictment, but it is relevant when it comes to the credibility of the witness and the termination of his service in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree. I think it's part of the whole story about this witness, Your Honour, and I'm not opposed to it being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if we understand the purpose for which you are relying on this Official Note, it would be in our view premature to tender it at this stage. It may very well be, depending on what happens as we progress, that there may be a basis on which it then becomes relevant to the credibility as you've indicated of this witness. But at this point it is, on the face of it, wholly irrelevant to the issues, to the live issues before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours. I'm actually asking for the instruction whether we should perhaps MFI the document or just leave it like as it is, and then if the -- if the issue is raised, then I can re-address this issue during my re-direct examination. I believe probably that would be the course to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness had indicated he wanted to make a fuller explanation about it. If you hear that now, then that may change your mind about whether it's timely to perhaps admit this or mark it MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I -- that did occur to me, Mr. Hannis, but speaking entirely for myself, I abandoned that for the simple reason that, as I later explained, whatever the explanation is, useful though it may be, it's all irrelevant at this point to the issues before us. That may come. And I agree with Mr. Zecevic that so that we keep track of these things, we could mark it for identification and leave it at that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 1D568, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Judge Harhoff dissenting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, did you return this poker machine where you had taken it from on the 28th of August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show to the witness 65 ter 179D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andan, this is an Official Note drafted on 28 August 1992. We read that the Official Note was submitted by ... and your signature below that. Is this your Official Note?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this Official Note you state that on 18 August 1992 you were summoned to Belgrade by the minister of the interior Mico Stanisic to discuss the departure to Foca with part of the special purposes unit. Since we have seen your notes and we saw them at the outset of today's work, you said then that you don't know whether there was a discussion with the minister. Do you remember now that it took place on the 28th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an Official Note and it -- well, there's no mistake about it. It certainly was the way it was written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the date of this meeting is important, and I wish to establish that by tendering this document, unless the Trial Chamber would prefer a different course of action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could you assist us in trying to elucidate what this document can offer in terms of evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you will remember that when we saw the witness's notes at the beginning of today's session, the witness testified that he met -- that he went on request of Mico Stanisic and met with him in Belgrade where he was given instructions for the operation to be conducted in Foca regarding the paramilitaries and the problems with the paramilitaries over there. One of the questions I posed to him was what instructions were given to him on that particular occasion by the minister, and the witness testified about that. I can give you the reference of the transcript if you give me some time. Now, the problem -- the problem is that his notes, his notebook where he was writing the notes, does not contain the date of this meeting in Belgrade with Mr. Stanisic. And I just wanted -- I just want to establish which date it was when Mr. Mico Stanisic, the minister, met with Mr. Andan, with the witness, and gave him the instructions to go to Foca and deal with the paramilitary units over there. That is the only purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But now we have the witness's testimony on the record. Isn't that sufficient? Do we need an extra document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is exactly the instructions I was seeking from the Trial Chamber. If the Trial Chamber is satisfied that it was sufficiently established that the meeting took place on the 18th of August, I'm not interested in offering this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I believe that the Chamber is fully satisfied with having the witness's testimony for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I, in general, also remind the parties that because of the overwhelming amount of evidence in this trial, the parties are required to show some restrictions or to show some caution not to seek to tender documents that are not strictly necessary, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is precisely why I seek the instruction from the Trial Chamber. Precisely for those reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to make an intervention here because at page 69, line 22, Mr. Zecevic's question is recorded: "Do you remember now that it took place on the 28th of August, 1992?" As I read the document, the meeting took place on the 18th. The document is dated the 28th. But Mr. Zecevic's question was the 28th and then the answer was: "... well, there's no mistake it about it. It certainly was the way it was written here." So it's not clear to me, so that's why I would not oppose to the document coming in. But if we clarify with the witness that the meeting was on the 18th, then if you don't want the document, I can live without it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, the Official Note, the date of the note, is 28, but -- or it is referred to -- the meeting, sir -- at line 17: "Sir, in this Official Note you state that on the 18th of August you were summoned to Belgrade ..." So I think it is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the transcript portion I was reading, Your Honour, was -- the question was: "Do you remember now that it took place on the 28th?" That's at page 69, line 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure I said 18th, but never mind. Just one question, and I see the time, or perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, let's tidy this up before we take the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andan, do you remember that this meeting with Mico Stanisic took place on the 18th of August 1992 in Belgrade as we see in this Official Note, on the 18th of August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR ANDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this Official Note is an official document, that there is no reason to doubt what it says. That meeting was held on the 18th of August, whereas the Official Note was drafted on the 28th of August. I was returning items that were -- had been issued to me, and I couldn't find some radios, and I contacted the man who had them, and that's why I mention this in the Official Note as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment until tomorrow. And we reconvene in Courtroom II at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of May, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
